Only `ConversionAgentTest.java` was added (the pre-existing `ConversionTest.java` deletion was already present before I started). All 115 tests pass.

**Summary:** Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/ConversionAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class (matching this project's style: `org.junit.jupiter.api`, `assertThrows`/`assertArrayEquals`, no inheritance from helper base classes). It covers all public static methods of `Conversion`:

- Bit/nibble conversions (`binaryBeMsb0ToHexDigit`, `binaryToHexDigit`, `binaryToHexDigitMsb0_4bits`, `hexDigit*` family, `intToHexDigit*`)
- Array↔primitive conversions (`binaryTo*`, `byteArrayTo*`, `shortArrayTo*`, `intArrayToLong`)
- Primitive→array/string conversions (`*ToBinary`, `*ToByteArray`, `*ToShortArray`, `*ToIntArray`, `*ToHex`)
- UUID round-trip (`uuidToByteArray`/`byteArrayToUuid`)
- Deprecated no-arg constructor

Each covers normal values, zero-count/early-return short circuits, and boundary/error cases (`IllegalArgumentException`, `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`, `NullPointerException`), including two regression tests for the int-overflow guard in the bounds checks (the fix from the most recent commit on this branch). Expected values for bit-shuffling methods were independently cross-checked with a scratch Python replica (outside the repo, since removed) rather than derived from the implementation itself, and I caught/fixed 9 incorrect boundary values in my initial draft this way before the suite went green.
